newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians storm port in bid to board foreign ship.
newsitem.headline: Albanians storm port in bid to board foreign ship.

text.p: Thousands of Albanians broke through police ranks at the port of Durres on Saturday in a desperate, failed attempt to escape the country on a Greek frigate evacuating Chinese and Iranian diplomats.
Police fired hundreds of warning shots into the air in an unsuccessful bid to hold the frenzied crowd back.
The unarmed civilians threw rocks and stones at the police and finally evaded the security cordon by climbing over, around and through a three-metre high wall at the port.
They ran through the port for some two km (a mile) to the end of the quay where the frigate was anchored, but by the time the stampede arrived the ship was steaming away.
About 5,000 mostly young Albanians, including families with infants in their arms, were left standing, sweating and winded -- cursing their fate and the local police.
"We have two options. either we take guns and kill these bastard police or we get a boat out of here," one young Albanian told reporters.
The melee began when cars and buses carrying diplomats and flying the Chinese and Iranian flags pulled up to the wrong gate at the port.
A crowd had already gathered there, drawn by the arrival of three Greek warships and the possibility of evacuation.
The Greek frigate was escorted by two torpedo boats, one of which pulled deep into the harbour. The crowd of would-be refugees screamed at the crew in Greek:
"Don't be afraid, come closer. Take us, take us away with you. We want to go to greece."
Government security forces in red and black ski masks, armed with Kalashnikov rifles, turned cars and buses from other parts of Albania away at the outskirts of Durres all day.
Those who rushed the Greek frigate included many residents of Durres and Albanians who had made their way to the city earlier in the week.

As the country's largest port, Durres is one of several staging points for the evacuation of foreigners following weeks of disorder ignited by anger at the government of President Sali Berisha, over the collapse of nine pyramid schemes which ruined many Albanians.

Most of those being evacuated from Durres on Saturday appeared to be Chinese diplomats and their families. It was the second consecutive day that the port had been the scene of wild scrambles among Albanians eager to flee.
Security forces appeared to be acting with restraint, firing into the air and avoiding using deadly force.
